newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Four accused in Bangladesh share scam surrender.
newsitem.headline: Four accused in Bangladesh share scam surrender.

text.p: Four of the 36 dealers and company owners facing arrest for alleged manipulation of share prices in Bangladesh's stock market have surrendered to the High Court and obtained bail, police said on Friday.
They include Salman Rahman, deputy chairman and three other top executives of his Beximco group of companies, who were granted "ad-interim bail" until Monday.
They will have to appear at the court of Dhaka's chief metropolitan magistrate (CMM) after Monday or seek to extend the bail from the High Court, police told reporters.
The arrest warrants were issued on Wednesday night by the CMM's court following cases filed against the 36 by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the capital market watchdog.

The SEC filed the cases on the basis on an inquiry, conducted by a four-member committee headed by professor Amirul Islam Chowdhury, which said the 36 dealers and company owners had been involved in "fraudulant activities" causing turbulence in share prices and losses to investors.
Police on Friday said the were still looking for the other 32 who had not surrendered to court.
A Beximco statement late on Thursday described the charges against its executives as "baseless, motivated, without fact and frivolous."
